Amends this group's 2026-10-25 trailing-comment carry (P300, queue 2026-10-30T09:41Z: 19 more lines refused or held in s7/s8). - `tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py` `parse_line` (77-90) drops a comment that starts at an unquoted word beginning with `#`, and only that: shell semantics. `tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py run` gains `--mark` (P300). - After each op's report line, the queue line it applied is rewritten in place as `#done <line>` when pushed (and the read-back did not print FAILED), else as `#refused <line>`. - The rewrite re-reads the queue file at write time and matches the exact line text, first unmarked occurrence. It writes through a temp file in the same directory and `os.replace`, so a line another writer appended after the run's first read is kept. - `run` with `--mark` also accepts `all` for FIRST..LAST, meaning every unmarked op line, so a seat needs no cursor. - Lines already starting with `#` (`#done`, `#refused`, `#held`, `#note`) are never applied, which is today's skip, now documented. - Basis: the s7 and s8 roster seats each wrapped the runner in an untracked loop (`roster-loop.sh` 90 lines, `roster-s8-loop.py` 111 lines) for this marking alone. The s8 `mark()` rewrites with `open(Q, 'w')` and no guard. - Self-test rows: - A pushed op marks `#done`; a refused op marks `#refused`. - A line appended to the queue between the run's first read and the mark survives. - Null: without `--mark` the queue file is byte-identical after the run. - One mutant: write the run-start snapshot instead of re-reading, and the appended-line row fails. triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch68.md#P300

From the s9 bulk roster apply (2026-11-01, roster 1d7ef52f..27e882736, 282 lines). Four defects found in the roster queue path, each measured:
(1) tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py line 7: the docstring gives the usage as `append-group <json-file>`, but argparse needs `append-group <GROUP> <json>`. 36 queue lines followed the docstring and were refused rc=2, along with every carry routed into those groups.
(2) roster_drain.py: its 3600 s timeout raises before any mark is written. A pass that runs over the timeout, as today's 62-push volume at 1-3 min each would have, loses every mark, and the next pass re-runs those lines.
(3) The drain skips any line containing ` #`, which strands valid ops whose quoted argument holds `#`, such as `#2257`. Four lines were stranded today.
(4) Throughput: one op, one lint and one push per line takes 1-3 min. The bulk path took 0.36 s per line: it called roster_edit main() for each line in a single worktree, with local commits, then ran lint_gate once and pushed once. The scripts are in the s9 scratchpad as bulk.py and readback_mark.py.
Fix: correct the docstring, with a self-test arm that runs the documented usage. Write marks incrementally, per line, as each op pushes. Parse the trailing-comment filter, don't substring-match it. Land a batched mode in roster_queue.py (`run --batch`) that reuses roster_edit's checks with one lint and one push, so instrument code doesn't live in /tmp. Failing test first: an arm for each of (1)-(3) that is red at main. Null control: a batch of one line gives a roster byte-identical to the single-op path's.

From the s9 script census: the roster seat's queue watcher is s7/roster-loop.sh (90 lines; the s8 copy is roster-s8-loop.py, 118 lines), and the triage seat's pass is s9/seat-triage/pass.sh; tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py (`run FIRST LAST`, `readback`) covers one pass but not what the loops carry. Four behaviours exist only in the shell loops: (1) marking: a landed queue line becomes `#done <line>`, a refused one `#refused <line>` (a refused op used to be consumed and never retried; a false refusal from an empty marker caused re-issues of landed ops); (2) flag parsing: --at-sha, --field, --match, --value, --over-cap are passed as flags and not folded into the positional value (set-stage X done --at-sha SHA once wrote stage="done --at-sha SHA", measured 2026-10-27 on R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE, and the plan held R10-ARCH-DOCS two days behind it); (3) the lint clone self-heals when its directory is missing; (4) `#held append-carry` lines are released when the batch file named in the carry exists on origin/main (pass.sh), with a LANDED/not-landed readback by the carry's first 60 characters against the roster JSON, and an `unwired open issue/PR` sweep escalates open numbers no live group owns. Fold into tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py: a `loop [--every 300]` subcommand using the existing runner, with the marking, the flag grammar (one shared parser for both the loop and `run`, so the asymmetry in queue line 24 cannot recur), the self-heal, `release-held` and the unwired sweep as separate subcommands. Planted control: a queue with one landing and one refused op ends with `#done` on the first and `#refused` on the second and the refused one is not retried; `set-stage G done --at-sha S` reaches roster_edit with stage `done` and the flag intact; a held line whose batch file is absent stays held. Mutation: fold the flag into the value and the second case must fail. Carry: R10-ORCH-ROSTER-SCHEMA
